title: Acute Limb Ischemia: The Six Ps and Time Sensitivity
subject: Surgical Triads

sections.title: Recognize the pattern
points: Acute limb ischemia is classically described by pain, pallor, pulselessness, paresthesia, paralysis and poikilothermia.
A threatened limb needs urgent vascular assessment; sensory or motor deficits indicate substantial ischemic risk.

sections.title: What this finding does—and does not—mean
points: Compare both limbs for temperature, color, capillary refill, pulses and Doppler signals.
Rapid assessment and appropriate anticoagulation or reperfusion planning depend on specialist evaluation.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not wait for all six signs; pulselessness may be difficult to assess and tissue damage is time-sensitive.
